title: An open box folded from a sheet of cardboard

stimulus.title: An open box
stimulus.text: A packaging designer makes an open box from a rectangular sheet of cardboard $30$ centimeters long and $20$ centimeters wide. She cuts a square with sides of $x$ centimeters from each corner and folds up the sides. The table gives the volume $V(x)$ of the box, in cubic centimeters, for selected values of $x$.

table.caption: Volume V(x) of the open box, in cubic centimeters, for cut size x, in centimeters

parts.label: A(i)
parts.prompt: Write an expression for $V(x)$, the volume of the box, in terms of $x$.

rubric.point: A correct product of the three dimensions

parts.sample: After the cuts, the base is $30 - 2x$ by $20 - 2x$ centimeters and the height is $x$ centimeters, so $V(x) = x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x)$.

parts.label: A(ii)
parts.prompt: Use your expression to find the cut size $x$ that gives the greatest volume, and the greatest volume. Give your answers correct to three decimal places.

rubric.point: Both values correct to three decimal places, with units

parts.sample: Graph $y = x(30 - 2x)(20 - 2x)$ for $0 < x < 10$ and use the maximum feature: $x \approx 3.924$ centimeters gives the greatest volume, $V \approx 1056.306$ cubic centimeters.

parts.label: B(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of $V$ on the interval $[1, 3]$, with units. Explain what this value represents on the graph of $V$.

rubric.point: The value $252$ cubic centimeters per centimeter, identified as the slope of the secant line through $(1, V(1))$ and $(3, V(3))$
accept: $\frac{1008 - 504}{3 - 1} = 252$ cubic centimeters per centimeter; it is the slope of the secant line through $(1, 504)$ and $(3, 1008)$

parts.sample: The average rate of change of $V$ on $[1, 3]$ is $\frac{V(3) - V(1)}{3 - 1} = \frac{1008 - 504}{2} = 252$ cubic centimeters per centimeter. It is the slope of the secant line through $(1, 504)$ and $(3, 1008)$ on the graph of $V$.

parts.label: B(ii)
parts.prompt: Use the secant line from part B(i) to estimate $V(2)$.

rubric.point: An estimate from a point on the secant line

parts.sample: The secant line is $y = 504 + 252(x - 1)$. At $x = 2$ it gives $504 + 252 = 756$, so $V(2) \approx 756$ cubic centimeters.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Is the estimate in part B(ii) an overestimate or an underestimate of $V(2)$? Give a reason for your answer.

rubric.point: Underestimate, with a reason from the concavity of $V$ on $[1, 3]$
accept: underestimate, because $V$ is concave down on $[1, 3]$, so the graph is above the secant line there
underestimate: the average rates on $[1, 2]$ and $[2, 3]$ are $328$ and $176$, decreasing, so $V$ is concave down on $[1, 3]$

parts.sample: An underestimate. On $[1, 3]$ the graph of $V$ is concave down: the average rates of change on $[1, 2]$ and $[2, 3]$ are $328$ and $176$ cubic centimeters per centimeter, which decrease. So the graph lies above the secant line on $[1, 3]$, and the secant line's value $756$ is below $V(2) = 832$.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: The designer uses the model $V$ only for values of $x$ that make sense in this context. Explain what the largest possible value of $x$ is, and why the model cannot be used past it.

rubric.point: The bound $x = 10$ (or $x < 10$) with a reason from the dimensions of the sheet
accept: $x < 10$, because the width $20 - 2x$ must be positive; at $x = 10$ the cuts use the whole $20$-centimeter width
for $x > 10$ the model uses a negative width $20 - 2x$, so its values (negative on $10 < x < 15$) describe no real box

parts.sample: $x$ must be less than $10$. The box's width is $20 - 2x$, which is $0$ at $x = 10$: the corner squares would use the whole width of the sheet, leaving no box. Past $x = 10$ the model uses a negative width (and gives negative volumes for $10 < x < 15$), which no real box has, so the context limits the domain to $0 < x < 10$.
